A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hybrid Preferences study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original performance-prediction, reward-model, and best-of-N experiments in Section 4, plus DPO experiments and Helpsteer2 analyses in Appendices I and K.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 2–4, the DPO results in Appendix I, and the Helpsteer2 experiments in Appendix K.

M1.justification: The tag-based feature representation, quadratic performance prediction model, candidate-generation algorithm, and simulation-based routing procedure in Section 2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same preference datasets, including Helpsteer2-Preferences in Appendix K.3, and the same RewardBench and downstream tasks. The newly mentioned CoAnnotating tasks belong to cited prior work, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The human-only, synthetic-only, random-mixture, regressor, and selection-strategy comparisons retain their comparator sets. CoAnnotating is added only to related work and is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: The 7K-instance preference mixes, 200 PPM training candidates, 16 held-out candidates, best-of-16 evaluation, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices G, I, and J.

E4.justification: The annotation-budget comparisons, tag-gain analysis, top-k versus simulated selection tests, and Helpsteer2 case studies are retained without revision, including Section 5 and Appendices E, F, and K.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run averaging statements, plotted error bars, and Appendix K agreement statistics. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-procedure changes are documented.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains MULTIPREF overall scores of 60.4, 66.5, and 70.6 for human-only, synthetic-only, and best-hybrid preferences; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The routing optimization in Equation 1, feature-vector definitions, and performance-gain calculations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about hybrid annotation quality, annotation efficiency, generalization, and identifying instances that benefit from human feedback.

C2.justification: Interpretations of human annotation benefits, ChatArena's downstream exception, and limitations concerning dataset scaling, feedback formats, and DPO/PPO generalization are unchanged. The limitations paragraph crossing a different page boundary is retained in full.

D1.justification: Annotation procedures, prompts, hyperparameters, TPU training details, and code/data access statements remain unchanged. The added NAIRR Pilot and Microsoft Azure acknowledgements credit support without specifying new implementation settings or access information.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds CoAnnotating (Li et al., 2023a), describing its uncertainty-guided human/LM allocation and distinguishing its downstream NLP tasks from preference annotation. Its reference is added; the AlpacaEval citation-letter changes identify the same existing works.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short related-work passage and expands the acknowledgements to credit NAIRR Pilot and Microsoft Azure. Citation suffixes and the arXiv version/date are updated; the remaining prose and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Added prose causes limited text reflow on pages 10–15, including splitting a limitations paragraph across pages 10–11 and shifting bibliography entries. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research positioning by acknowledging the closely related CoAnnotating framework and explaining its different annotation setting in Section 6, a connection absent from v1. The methods, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
